item.title: Province launches Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign on National Child Day
item.description:
Province launches Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign on National Child Day jenniferdhogan Fri, 11/20/2026 - 15:57

November 20th is National Child Day, an opportunity to recognize and celebrate the contributions of Island children and youth and reaffirm our shared commitment to their safety and well-being. 

As part of that commitment, the province is launching a new public awareness campaign to help Islanders better understand the Duty to Report law. Anyone who knows or suspects that the safety or well-being of a child is endangered must immediately contact Child Protection Services or the police.

“Keeping Island children safe and healthy is a responsibility shared by all of us. If you are concerned about a child, don’t wait. Make the call. Early action can help connect children and families with support.”

-Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

Through multilingual resources, public education sessions, and awareness efforts, the Don’t Wait, Make the Call campaign will increase understanding of when and how to report concerns and what happens after a report is made. 

“My department has worked closely with the Department of Social Development and Seniors to ensure policies and procedures across the education and early years systems align with the legal duty to report,” said Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher. “I believe the steps we are taking, including this valuable public education campaign, will improve safety for children across the province.”

With advocacy and support of the Office of the Child and Youth Advocate, the province passed legislation earlier this year that clarifies everyone’s legal responsibility to report concerns about a child’s safety and well-being.

“I welcome the department’s commitment to accepting recommendations from our Office to clarify and strengthen public knowledge regarding the duty to report,” said Marv Bernstein, Child and Youth Advocate. “When we collaborate, we can foster real and meaningful changes that directly uphold the rights of all children and youth to be protected from harm.” 

The 24/7 toll-free child protection phone number is 1 (877) 341-3101. To learn more about reporting, visit: Duty to Report

item.title: Public Schools Branch pilots video cameras on six school buses
item.description:
Public Schools Branch pilots video cameras on six school buses jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/19/2026 - 17:01

The Public Schools Branch (PSB) will begin testing video cameras on six school buses this week to improve safety for students and bus drivers and hold motorists accountable for illegally passing stopped buses.   

The pilot includes exterior cameras that record vehicles passing a stopped school bus while its red lights are flashing, and interior cameras that record video and audio inside the bus. Signs on each bus let riders know that cameras are in use.

"Drivers who pass a stopped school bus are putting children at serious risk," said PSB director of transportation and risk management Dave Gillis. "Our staff report these incidents to police, and we've heard again and again that video evidence would make those reports stronger. This pilot is about keeping everyone who uses our transportation system safe."

The interior cameras will help staff respond to behaviour concerns and incidents on buses fairly and accurately, supporting both students and drivers.

Along with this pilot, the PSB will finalize a policy on the use of video cameras on school buses.

                                                                 

Media contact:
Matt MacLeod
Public Schools Branch
mattimacleod@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder:

How footage is handled

  • Footage is not monitored live and is not reviewed routinely. It is only reviewed when an incident is reported.
  • Only branch-based transportation staff or school administrators may view footage.
  • Footage related to vehicles passing a stopped bus or incidents involving police may be shared with law enforcement as part of the report.
  • External camera footage is automatically deleted after 30 days unless it is needed for a reported incident.
  • Internal camera footage is automatically deleted after 90 days unless it is needed for a reported incident.

item.title: Statement by Minister Deagle on National Addictions Awareness Week
item.description:
Statement by Minister Deagle on National Addictions Awareness Week jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/19/2026 - 15:20

Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle issued the following statement: 

“National Addictions Awareness Week, November 15-21, is an opportunity to increase understanding, reduce stigma, and encourage conversations about substance use, gambling, and recovery. 

Addiction is a health issue that can affect anyone. Substance use and gambling-related harms impact individuals, families, workplaces, and communities across the province.

Reducing stigma is one of the most important ways we can help people access support. When people feel safe asking for help, they are more likely to seek treatment and begin their recovery journey. 

I would like to thank the health care professionals, addictions counsellors, peer support workers, outreach teams, first responders, and community organizations who support Islanders every day.

In Prince Edward Island, we continue to invest in a full range of services that help people prevent and address addiction, support recovery, and reduce harm. Islanders can also access counselling through Open Access Counselling clinics, support through the Mental Health and Addictions Phone Line, free naloxone kits through the Take Home Naloxone Program, and overdose monitoring through the National Overdose Response Service. 

During National Addictions Awareness Week, we reaffirm our commitment to ensuring Islanders feel safe asking for help and know that support is available. 

If you or someone you know is struggling with substance use, gambling, or addiction, please know that help is available and that you are not alone.

Call the Mental Health and Addictions phone line at 1-833-553-6983 for help 24 hours a day.”

item.title: Island artists celebrated at annual Arts Awards
item.description:
Island artists celebrated at annual Arts Awards jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/19/2026 - 15:06

Island artists were recognized for their excellence at the 2026 Prince Edward Island Arts Awards ceremony. 

The awards honour outstanding achievements in the arts and culture community. 

The following recipients were distinguished at the annual gala:

  • Artist of the Year Award: Logan Richard
  • Gertie & Henry Purdy Emerging Visual Arts Bursary: Alex Bevan-Baker  
  • Leo Cheverie Cultural Connector of the Year Award: Richard Pellissier-Lush
  • Organization of the Year Award: Club Red Productions  
  • Premier’s Award for Stand-Out Project of the Year: 333 - The Toronto Bathhouse Raids

“Congratulations to all of this year’s recipients on this well-deserved recognition. Island artists play an important role in shaping and strengthening our culture, and we are proud to support their creativity, talent and contributions to Prince Edward Island’s vibrant creative sector.”

- Minister of Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence Zack Bell


"What a thrill to be included among such a wealth of talented artists acknowledged at last night's awards ceremony. It was a beautiful celebration of a year of cultural excellence right here on PEI.  The team behind the production of 333 is so honoured by this recognition for our project and, importantly, so moved by this show of support for live, queer, and independent theatre that tells our Canadian stories. I couldn't be prouder of this accomplishment and to be a creative artist here in PEI.  This whole experience has been so wonderfully validating.  Thank you to everyone who made these awards happen."

- Premier's Award for Stand-Out Project of the Year recipient Jay Whitehead

"Receiving the Leo Cheverie Cultural Connector of the Year Award is an incredible honour, especially knowing the legacy of a man who dedicated his life to bringing people together. As a proud Mi'kmaw artist from Lennox Island First Nation, I believe the arts are more than performances or creative expression. They are opportunities to build bridges, preserve our stories, celebrate our identities, and create a sense of belonging. I share this recognition with my family, our Elders, our youth, and everyone who continues to support and uplift Indigenous voices. My greatest hope is that the work we do today inspires the next generation to embrace their culture, find their voice, and recognize that their stories deserve to be heard."

- Leo Cheverie Cultural Connector of the Year Award recipient Richard Pellissier-Lush

Each recipient receives a cash prize and a unique work of art created in Prince Edward Island. 

Learn more about the Prince Edward Island Arts Awards.

Media contact:
Jill Edwards
Department of Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence
jedwards@gov.pe.ca 

Backgrounder

  • The Leo Cheverie Cultural Connector of the Year Award: Celebrates an individual, group or organization from PEI whose role as a champion of the arts has had a positive impact on creating access and connections between various communities within the arts and culture sector of the province.
     
  • The Artist of the Year Award: Celebrates an individual artist or group regardless of artistic discipline who has had a break-out year in their respective field of practice and has demonstrated outstanding contribution and growth. Assessors will be looking for merit in artistic achievement, momentum for the future, professional recognition, as well as provincial, national and/or international recognition.
     
  • The Organization of the Year Award: Recognizes an organization from PEI whose artistic and cultural contributions have had a significant, positive impact on the provincial landscape, its residents, and visitors. Individuals, groups and bands are not considered organizations and should therefore be nominated under another category.  
     
  • The Premier of Prince Edward Island’s Award for Stand-Out Project of the Year: Recognizes an artist, arts professional, group, collective or arts organization that has produced an innovative artistic or cultural project addressing themes such as reconciliation, climate change, accessibility, digital innovation, and more.
     

  • The Gertie & Henry Purdy Emerging Visual Arts Bursary: Awarded to an emerging artist in the visual arts to support any activity that encourages training, promotion, exhibition, and leadership in and to the field of practice of the artist. This bursary is intended for creators in the plastic arts fields. Traditionally, these art forms include sculpture, drawing, painting, printmaking, ceramics, and photography. Filmmaking and media arts are not included.

     

  • The Father Adrien Arsenault Senior Arts Award (awarded bi-annually. The next prize in this category will be awarded in 2027): Honours and acknowledges the excellence of the work of a senior Island artist who has produced a significant body of work in the practice of visual arts, writing and publishing, music, dance, fine craft, theatre, film, or video.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
